title: The Last Inheritance Again
premise: True-crime podcaster Noor Voss built her reputation on closing cases, so when a confession letter for the forty-year-old Voss family inheritance murder arrives postmarked the day after its last witness's funeral — signed with her own estranged mother's name — she can't resist. Following the letter's clues to the decaying Voss estate, Noor discovers a household ledger whose innocuous entries encode the real chain of custody of the inheritance, implicating the found-family of servants who raised her alongside the blood relatives who disowned her. As the anniversary dinner approaches and someone begins quietly eliminating ledger-keepers, Noor must choose between exposing the truth that will destroy her chosen family or burying it and becoming complicit. In the end she broadcasts the decoded ledger live from the dinner itself, letting loyalty and truth collide publicly — and learns her mother confessed to protect Noor, taking the fall for a crime the whole household committed together.
about_author: Felix Almeida is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing estate papers and probate disputes before turning to fiction. They write mysteries obsessed with paperwork, inheritance, and the lies families tell in ledgers.

chapters.title: Postmarked Yesterday
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. A confession letter arrives naming her mother in a forty-year-old murder, postmarked one day after the witness's funeral. Noor, who never takes a case she can't close, plays the letter on air as bait. Emotional beat: professional confidence cracking into personal dread.

chapters.title: The House That Kept Books
chapters.summary: Noor POV. She returns to the Voss estate, now half-inn, half-museum, run by Marisol, the former housekeeper who helped raise her. The welcome is warm but watchful; her childhood bedroom is preserved like a shrine. Beat: the seduction of belonging versus the itch of suspicion.

chapters.title: Entries in a Dead Hand
chapters.summary: Alternating Noor and Marisol POVs. Noor finds the old household ledger; Marisol privately burns a page. The entries look mundane — flour, lamp oil, 'payment rendered' — but dates cluster around the murder. Beat: dread disguised as domestic routine.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Guest List
chapters.summary: Noor POV. Invitations go out for the fortieth-anniversary dinner; every guest is a former servant or heir, every one a possible ledger-keeper. Old groundskeeper Teodor warns her to leave. Beat: paranoia blooms inside nostalgia.

chapters.title: What Mother Never Said
chapters.summary: Marisol POV. Flashbacks interleave with present: the night of the murder, seen through a young servant's eyes, and the pact made afterward to protect a child — Noor. Beat: sympathy curdling into complicity.

chapters.title: A Missing Page and a Missing Man
chapters.summary: Noor POV. Teodor disappears; his room holds a duplicate ledger key — a cipher of initials and sums. Someone searched it before her. Beat: the case stops being cold and starts being dangerous.

chapters.title: The Cipher at the Bottom of the Page
chapters.summary: Noor POV, late-night intensity. She cracks the code: each 'purchase' maps to a payment, each payment to a person, tracing the inheritance through every hand at the estate — including Marisol's and her own mother's. Beat: triumph immediately poisoned by what it reveals.

chapters.title: Glass Half Empty
chapters.summary: Marisol POV. On dinner eve, Marisol confronts whoever has been silencing witnesses and fails; a second ledger-keeper is found dead. She decides Noor must be protected from the truth — even if that means lying again. Beat: love weaponized into concealment.

chapters.title: The Toast
chapters.summary: Noor POV. At the anniversary dinner, glasses rise, secrets tighten, and Noor goes live on air, reading the decoded ledger aloud as the room freezes. The killer lunges; Marisol steps between them. Beat: climax — truth spoken at the exact moment loyalty demands silence.

chapters.title: Settled Accounts
chapters.summary: Noor POV, then coda. The killer — the estate lawyer who forged the original will — confesses; the servants' shared guilt dissolves into shared grief. Noor airs her mother's full story, closes the case, and redefines family as those who stay for the reckoning. Beat: bittersweet resolution, accounts finally balanced.
